## Religion and the state: how far apart a constitution puts them

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/religion-and-the-state/

The very first line of Article 29 of Indonesia's constitution is that the state is based upon belief in the One and Only God. Brazil's Article 19 runs the other way, forbidding the Union, the states and the municipalities to establish religions, subsidise them, or maintain relations of dependence or alliance with them. Japan's Article 20 goes further into detail — no religious organisation may take privileges from the state, and public authorities are kept out of religious teaching and observance altogether — with Article 89 barring public money from religious bodies. The American First Amendment says Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion. China's Article 36 guarantees freedom of belief but protects "normal religious activities" and states that religious affairs are not subject to foreign domination. India's preamble calls the republic secular, while Article 25 includes the right to *propagate* religion. Taiwan's Article 13 is seven characters long: the people have freedom of religious belief.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/religion-and-the-state/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/religion-and-the-state/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/religion-and-the-state/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/religion-and-the-state/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/religion-and-the-state/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/religion-and-the-state/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/religion-and-the-state/us/)

## Rental deposits and landlord power: how many months, and how easily they can end it

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/renting-a-home/

Taiwan's Housing Rental Market Development and Management Act caps the deposit at two months' rent (Article 7) and lists five grounds on which a landlord may end the lease early (Article 10) — four require thirty days' written notice, reclaiming the unit for reconstruction requires three months'. Mainland China's Housing Rental Regulation (State Council Order No. 812, in force since 15 September 2025) only requires the deposit amount, refund timing and deduction grounds to be written into the contract — it sets no cap at all. Japan's Civil Code Article 622-2 requires a landlord to refund the *shikikin* (security deposit), minus what the tenant owes, once the lease ends and the unit is returned; Japan additionally has *reikin* — "key money" paid to the landlord, usually non-refundable, that no statute requires or limits — and the Land and House Lease Act's Article 28 requires "just cause" before a landlord may refuse renewal or terminate, so a tenant cannot simply be told to leave. The United States has no federal rule at all: HUD's role is limited to anti-discrimination under the Fair Housing Act, and deposit caps are set state by state — California's Civil Code §1950.5, as amended by AB 12 (effective July 2024), cut the limit from two or three months to one. India's Model Tenancy Act, 2021 is only a template for states to adopt — it proposes a two-month cap for residential premises, six for commercial — but most states still run on their own older Rent Control Acts. Indonesia's rental law still traces to the Dutch-era Civil Code (Articles 1548 onward); the deposit amount is left entirely to contract, and a landlord cannot evict a tenant who refuses to leave without going through court. Brazil's Tenancy Law caps the deposit at three months' rent, held in a savings account (Article 38), while Article 46 lets a landlord reclaim the unit without cause once a contract of thirty months or longer expires.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/renting-a-home/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/renting-a-home/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/renting-a-home/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/renting-a-home/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/renting-a-home/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/renting-a-home/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/renting-a-home/us/)

## How many days to register a residence permit — and does a new address or a new job have to be reported?

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/residency-and-visas/

Taiwan's Alien Resident Certificate, issued by the National Immigration Agency, must be applied for within 30 days of entry, and an address change reported within the same 30-day window — miss it and the Immigration Act sets a fine of NT$2,000–10,000. Japan's Residence Card runs on a tighter clock: 14 days, whether it's the first address registration or notifying a change of employer, both fixed by the Immigration Control Act. Mainland China gives registered residence-permit changes 10 days (Exit-Entry Administration Law, Article 33), and staying somewhere other than a hotel only 24 hours (Article 39). The United States has no national residence-registration office at all, but a registered alien's change of address is still bound by federal law — 8 U.S.C. § 1305 — to the same 10-day window, in writing. India runs on visa category rather than a single residence card: an Employment or Student visa valid over 180 days must be registered with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival. Indonesia caps an address change at 14 days, with the sponsor jointly responsible for reporting it. Brazil is the most generous: a temporary-visa holder has 90 days to register with the Federal Police. On whether the work permit and the residence permit are the same document, the seven countries split two ways: Taiwan, China, and Indonesia issue two documents from two agencies; Japan builds work eligibility directly into the residence status itself; and in the United States, the Green Card is itself the proof of work authorization.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/residency-and-visas/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/residency-and-visas/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/residency-and-visas/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/residency-and-visas/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/residency-and-visas/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/residency-and-visas/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/residency-and-visas/us/)

## Shopping Festivals

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/shopping-festivals/

Shopping festivals are the one kind of festival the retail trade invented for itself and the state had to regulate afterwards. Federal law in the United States knows Thanksgiving but has never heard of Black Friday. China's market regulator writes to the platforms every year and fixes the reference price for a discount at the lowest transaction price of the previous seven days. Indonesia's Harbolnas carries the trade ministry's name, and the minister himself sells on livestream. India regulates not the discount but the interface. Buy the same thing on the same day and the answer to "can I send it back, for how long, and who pays the postage" is different in every market.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/shopping-festivals/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/shopping-festivals/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/shopping-festivals/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/shopping-festivals/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/shopping-festivals/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/shopping-festivals/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/shopping-festivals/us/)

## Tanabata and Qixi

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/tanabata-and-qixi/

One legend about a weaver and a herdsman, one date in the seventh lunar month, and three societies that made three different festivals out of it. Taiwan keeps it on the lunar calendar and stacks two things on the same day — a couples' evening and a coming-of-age rite in Tainan. China registered it as national intangible heritage but left it off even the list of days explicitly named as non-holidays. Japan moved it onto 7 July when the country switched calendars in 1873, while Sendai pushed it a month later to 6–8 August. This page compares where the day sits in law, who gets time off, and what each place kept of the story.

- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/tanabata-and-qixi/cn/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/tanabata-and-qixi/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/tanabata-and-qixi/tw/)
- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/tanabata-and-qixi/br/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/tanabata-and-qixi/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/tanabata-and-qixi/in/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/tanabata-and-qixi/us/)

## Teachers' Day

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/teachers-day/

In 2027, the dates on this page are India on 5 September, mainland China on 10 September, Taiwan on 28 September, Brazil on 15 October, Indonesia on 25 November, Singapore on 3 September (estimated from the school calendar), and the United States' Teacher Appreciation Week on 3–7 May, with local district dates varying. Only Taiwan makes Teachers' Day a national day off; the other dates are commemorative or school-community observances. The page then explains why each place chose its date.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/teachers-day/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/teachers-day/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/teachers-day/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/teachers-day/in/)

## What voting asks of you, country by country

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/voting-and-elections/

Article 14 of Brazil's constitution makes voting a duty for citizens between eighteen and seventy, and you must account for missing it. Taiwan's Public Officials Election and Recall Act says in Article 17 that you vote at the polling station of your household registration — there is no absentee ballot, so election day becomes an island-wide journey home. China's constitution reserves direct election for the county and township level. And in the United States, federal law fixes election day as the Tuesday after the first Monday in November — a day that is not a holiday. One act, seven different answers to who may vote, where, and whether the day belongs to you.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/voting-and-elections/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/voting-and-elections/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/voting-and-elections/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/voting-and-elections/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/voting-and-elections/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/voting-and-elections/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/voting-and-elections/us/)

## War dead and veterans

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/war-dead-and-veterans/

The United States splits the dead from the survivors into two separate federal holidays: Memorial Day in May for those killed, Veterans Day on 11 November for those who came home. The other six countries mostly set aside a single day, and mostly do not give it off — Taiwan lets the defence ministry decide who gets the day, Japan's 15 August rests on a cabinet decision rather than any statute, and Indonesia's Heroes' Day is filed by presidential decree under "national days that are not holidays".

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/war-dead-and-veterans/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/war-dead-and-veterans/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/war-dead-and-veterans/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/war-dead-and-veterans/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/war-dead-and-veterans/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/war-dead-and-veterans/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/war-dead-and-veterans/us/)

## Weddings and Marriage Customs

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/weddings-and-customs/

The legal doorway to marriage differs by place. Taiwan requires household-registration entry for the marriage to take effect; Japan forms the marriage when the marriage notification is accepted; Brazil centres civil registration; Indonesia commonly layers religious ceremony and state registration; India offers personal-law routes alongside the Special Marriage Act; mainland China sets the minimum age at 22 for men and 20 for women; and US marriage licences are handled by the states. A ceremony, banquet, and legal registration may happen on different days. This guide separates legal marriage from the wedding celebration before comparing family and local customs.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/weddings-and-customs/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/weddings-and-customs/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/weddings-and-customs/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/weddings-and-customs/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/weddings-and-customs/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/weddings-and-customs/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/weddings-and-customs/us/)

## International Women's Day

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/womens-day/

March 8 falls on the same day in all seven places compared here, and is treated completely differently by each legal system. China gives women a paid half-day, written into the State Council's holiday regulation. Taiwan lists it as a "festival" but its statute states plainly that it is not a day off. The United States does not use the single date at all, designating all of March as Women's History Month. Brazil is the odd one out: its national women's day sat on April 30 until a 2025 law moved it to March 8. What this page compares is not who values women more, but how far each system formally recognises the same date.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/womens-day/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/womens-day/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/womens-day/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/womens-day/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/womens-day/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/womens-day/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/womens-day/us/)

## Year-End Bonus and the Thirteenth Salary

https://en.aeiou.now/topic/year-end-bonus/

Taiwan's year-end bonus rests on Article 29 of the Labor Standards Act, which applies only when the business closes its year with a surplus — a condition, with no deadline and no penalty, so the amount is the company's call. Brazil is the opposite: the thirteenth salary has been a statutory obligation since 1962, first instalment by 30 November and second by 20 December, with fines for lateness. Indonesia's THR must be paid in full seven days before the religious holiday, never in instalments, with a 5 per cent fine if late. The same idea — extra money once a year — runs from binding law to pure custom across the seven markets, and that is what decides whether anyone can rely on it.

- [Brazil](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/year-end-bonus/br/)
- [China](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/year-end-bonus/cn/)
- [Indonesia](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/year-end-bonus/id/)
- [India](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/year-end-bonus/in/)
- [Japan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/year-end-bonus/jp/)
- [Taiwan](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/year-end-bonus/tw/)
- [United States](https://en.aeiou.now/topic/year-end-bonus/us/)
